ritual: naming, anointing, or presentation of a token of office

If the invocation binds two subjects in a compact, both also gain +10 TN on Willpower tests to resist coercion, fear, or temptation to abandon it. Creatures attempting to countermand the subject through false claims or deliberate misrepresentation suffer -10 TN on the relevant Persuade or Deceive test. name: Fortune In Circulation
ritual: naming of the two fates before witness or shrine
duration: Permanent until reversed by miracle, invocation, or extraordinary means

text.raw:
The invoker causes the luck of two subjects to pass into one another's keeping. One subject may be the invoker. If both subjects are willing, the exchange is resolved automatically once the invocation succeeds. If either subject is unwilling, that subject may resist with an Opposed Luck test; if the target has no Luck score or the GM deems another defense more appropriate, use Willpower instead. On a successful exchange, the subjects permanently exchange their current Luck characteristic scores. Recalculate each subject's Luck Bonus, Luck Point maximum, and all other effects that depend on their current Luck. Any previously burned or reduced Luck is part of the exchanged value, because the rite transfers present fortune, not original birthright. Current LP totals are then adjusted to the new owners of that fortune; if either total would exceed the new LP maximum, reduce it to that maximum.

DoS 4+: The exchange is clean and complete. In addition to the above, each subject also exchanges their current allotment of Lucky and Unlucky Numbers as part of the transferred fortune. If one subject was unwilling and the invoker won the opposed test, that subject also suffers -10 TN on their next Luck or Willpower test before the next dawn.
DoS 1-3: The exchange succeeds as above, but Lucky and Unlucky Numbers do not transfer; instead, each subject immediately rerolls the appropriate set of Lucky and Unlucky Numbers for their new Luck Bonus.
DoF 4+: Fortune recoils on the invoker. The intended exchange fails, and the invoker permanently loses 1 Luck. If one target was unwilling, that target immediately gains 1 LP if able.

name: Exorcism
ritual: prayer, chanting, use of ritually prepared appropriate Domain materials

text.raw: The invoker contests the hold of a spirit, haunting presence, bound shade, possessing entity, or similar incorporeal claimant over a subject, object, corpse, or bounded place. The rite does not assume the spirit is evil, rightful, or wrongful; it establishes which will prevails in the present moment. The rite must be performed either on ritually prepared ground or with ritually prepared materials aligned to the invoker's Domain. The invoker declares one intended outcome before the test: Expel, Bind, Pacify, or Transfer. The invoker then makes a Ritual [Domain] test opposed by the entity's Magic test, or Willpower if it has no Magic. If the target is a willing possessed subject, that subject may aid the invoker; if the spirit is invited or lawfully anchored there, the GM may grant it a bonus or rule the rite inapplicable. Expel: The spirit is forced out of the subject, object, corpse, or place and cannot re-enter for the duration set by the result. Bind: The spirit remains present but is constrained, unable to possess, manifest violently, or act beyond the limits stated by the invoker. Pacify: The spirit is not driven out, but its active hostility, torment, compulsion, or intrusive influence is suppressed. Transfer: The spirit is removed from its current seat and compelled into a prepared valid receptacle, vessel, corpse, locus, or bounded area designated during the rite. The rite cannot transfer a spirit into an unwilling living host unless some other effect or prior condition explicitly allows it. DoS 4+: The declared outcome succeeds fully. If Expel was chosen, the spirit cannot return to the same target ever again, unless a greater power, miracle, or explicit counter-rite overcomes this ban. If Bind or Pacify was chosen, the constraint lasts indefinitely until broken. If Transfer was chosen, the transfer is clean and the spirit cannot immediately escape by ordinary means. DoS 1-3: The declared outcome succeeds. If Expel was chosen, the spirit is removed but may attempt to return after one lunar month or after the ward is broken, at GM discretion. If Bind or Pacify was chosen, the effect lasts until next dawn, one lunar cycle, or another fitting finite duration set by the GM. If Transfer was chosen, the spirit is moved successfully, but the new confinement is imperfect and may later be tested or broken. DoF 4+: The rite backfires. The spirit immediately lashes out, strengthens its hold, or twists the declared outcome. The invoker, the primary subject, or both must test Willpower +0 or suffer a severe manifestation appropriate to the entity and Domain: Panic, Fatigue, Dazed, temporary muteness, paralysis, intrusive visions, loss of memory, involuntary speech, or another similar affliction. If Transfer was declared, the spirit may instead erupt uncontrolled into the surrounding area or seize the nearest vulnerable valid host, at GM discretion
